mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.2%) signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.5%) over the past three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving averages indicates weakening economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both below 12-month moving average
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both INDPRO and HOUST are below 12-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a high interest rate regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to elevated discount rates and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) signal increased consumer confidence and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST rises (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI increase exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%) signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.2% from the prior month indicates weakening labor and consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both decline > 0.2% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both PAYEMS and RSAFS decline > 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
